messages:
Talia (networking): quick note from today's spike: ENI attach latency kills tail latency for cold traffic. proposing a "warm pool" model and a deterministic failover contract.
Jared (infra): agree re cold starts. what's the warm pool? pre-attached ENIs sitting idle in customer account? that sounds expensive and has quota implications.
Talia (networking): not full ENIs per se. two variants: (1) warm ENIs = pre-created ENIs with minimal config ready to register as targets, (2) warm agents = tiny daemon always attached but not registering until we flip a flag. both trade cost vs attach time.
Priya (security): any pre-provisioning in a customer account increases our attack surface. we must ensure minimal IAM, short-lived creds, and an auditable creation flow. no long-lived keys left behind.
Liam (product): customers care about two things: consistent low latency on burst and clear billing. if warm pool increases their monthly spend we need to surface it and make it opt-in.
Talia (networking): propose defaults: relay-only for everyone. warm-pool opt-in for customers that enable eni-preferred. warm-pool paid feature (metered as reserved ENI-hours) or pass-through billing.
Jared (infra): operationally we need logic: warm allocation per account = min(max(1, floor(baseline_rps/1000)), account_eni_quota-2). control plane will suggest pool size; customer can override.
Priya (security): handshake flow must be explicit: customer runs our terraform snippet which creates a limited role + an SSM parameter to record pool intent. our controller assumes role with STS:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity or similar and only creates warm resources. delete flow must be atomic and leave no leftover resources.
Talia (networking): failover contract: TTL for route/cache = 45s. On attach failure or health loss, control plane flips registration to central relay within 2 intervals. We must document observable signals and expected RTO.
Jared (infra): add metrics we need from agent: attach_time_ms, attach_failures_total, warm_pool_count, register_count, health_last. instrument control plane to alert if attach_failures_rate > 0.5% over 5m.
Liam (product): add a customer-visible dashboard: warm_pool_cost_estimate, average_attach_time, failover_events_count. add UI toggle: auto-warm vs manual warm.
Priya (security): certs & keys: agent should only use ephemeral session tokens. For mTLS bootstrap we can rely on KMS-signed short-lived certs. key rotation policy: rotate every 6h by default. document incident playbook for a compromised agent.
Talia (networking): snippet we discussed for terraform (skeletal):
```
# customer opt-in snippet
resource "aws_iam_role" "redwood_agent" {
  name = "redwood-ep-agent-${var.customer_id}"
  assume_role_policy = file("assume.json")
}
resource "redwood_optin" "warm_pool" {
  customer_id = var.customer_id
  desired_warm = var.warm_count
}
```
Jared (infra): regression tests: simulate attach spike under 50k rps and validate that warm pool reduces p99 by X%. we need an e2e harness that can run in a sandbox customer account.
Liam (product): rollout plan: beta with 3 customers, measure p99 improvement and billing delta, then GA with explicit opt-in + docs. Pricing note: recommend a small monthly surcharge OR per-hour reserved ENI pricing.
Priya (security): include a compliance checklist: IAM review, cert rotation, audit log retention >=90d, and an emergency revoke flow.
ci-bot: created ticket RED-2981 with checklist: "warm-pool RFC + tests + terraform examples"
Talia (networking): RFC TODOs: define exact warm-pool semantics, agent API for health & lifecycle, control plane allocation algorithm, UI/price language, and rollback playbook. I'll draft and tag infra/security/product.
Jared (infra): one more: header propagation must be explicit in the contract. if client ip preserved we set X-Forwarded-For; if SNATed we add X-Original-Client when known. add x-redwood-hop-count for tracing.
Liam (product): good catch. we'll include header examples in docs and a note about downstream fingerprint differences.
Talia (networking): ok wrapping up. aim to have RFC draft by Wednesday. thanks all. :rocket:
